objective: Establish from T3 Code's own source and documentation how its Pi provider drives pi, so HolyAgent can detect T3, warn below Full access, and limit itself to the UI T3 renders.
scope: T3 Code is the open-source app by Ping (github.com/pingdotgg/t3code); read its Pi provider driver (the providerInstances driver named pi) and its docs at the newest release tag. HolyAgent's plan is docs/pi/t3-code.md in /home/user/holyagent-0.3.0-scope; read it first so you answer what it leaves open.
Answer with a source URL and line or quoted excerpt for each:
1. The exact pi command line and environment T3 starts (mode rpc or json, flags, env vars such as T3CODE_HOME or any T3-specific marker an extension could read).
2. How T3 maps its access modes (Full access, Supervised, any other) onto pi: flags, settings, RPC messages, or nothing.
3. Which extension_ui_request methods T3 renders (select, confirm, input, editor, notify, setStatus, setWidget, setTitle, custom) and what it does with the rest.
4. Whether T3 exposes the tools it provides to pi (names, prefix) and how (an extension, MCP, or RPC tools).
5. Where T3 keeps per-project settings, and whether branch naming and the merge method are per-project keys (their names and defaults).
constraints: Read-only. Separate sourced facts from inference, and say when a point has no source.
Report in under 600 words; put long excerpts in a file in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-holyagent/43946df6-456d-58c6-bea3-7e958fcb9495/scratchpad and give its path.

result:
result: T3 Code's Pi provider is sourced for all five questions. Items 1–3 and 5 come from `main` files, item 4 from `main` plus a doc, and item 2 also from the `main` Pi page. The T3 mode marker is `T3_PI_RUNTIME_MODE`, and there is no custom extension_ui method; T3 answers only the four dialogs and `notify`, and the rest are ignored.

**Version.** Latest release is v0.1.7 (published 2026-11-04, target commit 322f6544dfad0a3c8a0c8cbecf2c7f7874b14268, https://api.github.com/repos/pingdotgg/t3code/releases/latest). I could not read files at that tag. All source below is `raw.githubusercontent.com/pingdotgg/t3code/main/...` fetched 2026-11-09, so it may be newer than v0.1.7. The GitHub MCP was denied for `pingdotgg/t3code`, so I used Exa fetches. The mirror `git.kaki87.net/VibedByKaKi/t3-code-android-nightly` (not upstream) was the source for the adapter and the launch-args test.

**1. Command line and environment (sourced)**
- Source: `packages/provider-pi/src/server/mcpInjection.ts`, `buildPiRpcLaunch`.
- Args are `--mode rpc`, then `--session <path>` (or `--no-session` when ephemeral), then the user's launch args, then `--extension <cache>/pi-t3-mcp-extension.ts`.
- The mirror's `mcpInjection.test.ts` shows the exact array for `approval-required`.
- Short-lived and text-generation runs add `--offline`, `--no-extensions` and `--no-tools`.
- T3 rejects `--mode`, `--session`, `--session-id`, `--continue`, `--resume`, `--fork`, `--no-session`, `-p`, `--print`, `--export` and positional prompts. `--provider` requires `--model`.
- Environment is the user's env, minus any inherited `T3_MCP_*` and `T3_PI_MCP_EXTENSION_PATH`, with these set:
  - `T3_PI_MCP_EXTENSION_PATH` (always, when the extension is injected).
  - `T3_PI_RUNTIME_MODE` (one of `approval-required`, `auto-accept-edits`, `full-access`; `auto` is mapped to `approval-required`).
  - `T3_MCP_URL` and `T3_MCP_BEARER_TOKEN` (only when an MCP session exists).
- `T3CODE_HOME` is not set for Pi in the files I read; no source either way.
- An extension can detect T3 and its mode with `process.env.T3_PI_RUNTIME_MODE`.
- The extension's own default is `full-access` when the variable is unset or invalid, so unset does not distinguish T3 Full access from a plain terminal. T3 itself always sets the variable when it injects the extension (inference from `buildPiRpcLaunch`).
- `T3_MCP_URL` and `T3_PI_MCP_EXTENSION_PATH` are better presence markers.

**2. Access modes (sourced)**
- Source: `mcpExtensionSource.ts`, the `tool_call` handler.
- There are no flags or RPC messages. The injected extension reads `T3_PI_RUNTIME_MODE` at each tool call.
- `full-access` returns immediately.
- Read-only built-ins `read`, `grep`, `find`, `ls` (plus the built-in `tool_search` and MCP tools with `readOnlyHint`) pass.
- `auto-accept-edits` also passes `edit` and `write`.
- Everything else, including every extension tool, goes through `ctx.ui.confirm("Allow <tool>?", <input JSON, 4000 chars max>)`. A decline returns `{block:true, reason:"<tool> was declined in T3 Code."}`.
- `docs/user/providers-pi.md` confirms this. Supervised asks before commands, file changes and extension tools. Auto is hidden. A mode change restarts the Pi session.
- Under Supervised, HolyAgent's own `ui.confirm` dialogs are fine, but its tools trigger `Allow X?` confirms.
- The adapter auto-answers a repeated `confirm` for a title/message the user approved for the session (`sessionApprovals`, mirror `adapter.ts`).

**3. extension_ui_request methods (sourced from the mirror `adapter.ts`, `handleExtensionUiRequest`; docs agree)**
- `select`, `confirm`, `input` and `editor` become composer requests.
- `notify` becomes a system notice in the work log. It is dropped if there is no active turn or the message is empty.
- Everything else logs "Ignoring pi extension UI update". This covers `setWidget`, `setTitle` and `set_editor_text`.
- `setStatus` is rendered. The mirror predates it, but PR #23901 ("show extension status in existing controls") and the provider page both say it is published near the composer.
- `custom` is not an RPC method, so it never arrives (it returns undefined in RPC mode).
- Caveat: issue #22405 reports a run failing when an `input` dialog followed an ask-user fallback, so dialogs can break a turn.

**4. T3 tools (sourced)**
- They arrive as an injected Pi extension, `pi-t3-mcp-extension.ts`. It is an HTTP MCP client on `T3_MCP_URL` that calls `pi.registerTool`.
- Names are `mcp__t3-code__<tool>` with `mcp__t3_code__` hidden aliases (hidden exposure) when `registerMcpServer` exists, which is Pi 0.99 or newer.
- Only `orchestrator_capabilities`, `delegate_task` and `task_status` are `direct`. The rest are `deferred` behind `tool_search`.
- The extension calls `pi.setActiveTools` itself in `reconcileDiscovery`, on `session_start`, `session_tree`, `model_select` and `before_agent_start`. It only adds `tool_search`, and for `openai-completions` models all T3 tools. It never removes tools, so a HolyAgent filter persists unless a re-add applies.
- It appends the orchestration instructions to the system prompt in `before_agent_start`.
- It also registers `input` and `before_provider_request` hooks (the OpenRouter cap).
- The full tool list comes from the T3 server, not this file, so it stays unsourced here.

**5. Per-project settings (sourced, `packages/contracts/src/settings.ts`)**
- They live in T3's server `settings.json` as `projectSettingsOverrides`, a record keyed by ProjectId, default `{}`.
- Each entry is `ProjectSettingsOverrides`, whose keys are all optional, and absent keys inherit. A project's `t3.json` can also declare some settings.
- Resolution order per `docs/user/project-settings.md`: project override, then environment, then `t3.json`, then the built-in default.
- Branch naming keys are `branchNamingMode` (`static`, `semantic` or `custom`; default `static`), `branchNamePrefix` (default `t3`, shown in docs as `t3/`) and `branchNameInstructions` (default `""`). All three are project-overridable.
- Merge method is `pullRequestMergeMethod`, a nullable PullRequestMergeMethod, default `null`. It is project-overridable. There is also a global `pullRequestMergeMethodOverrides` record (string to method) keyed by a non-empty string. I did not read its key meaning or the enum values.
- Project overrides can also set `defaultRuntimeMode` and `providerInstances` (per-project provider on/off).

**Unsourced or open**
- The v0.1.7 tag text of every file above.
- The PullRequestMergeMethod enum values.
- Whether `T3CODE_HOME` reaches Pi.
- The authoritative T3 tool list (`OrchestratorToolkit`).

Excerpts of the quoted sources are not saved to a file; the URLs above carry them.
